articles.title: Game over? How playing Grand Theft Auto VI is affecting elite athletes’ performances | Sean Ingle
articles.summary: Burning the midnight oil playing video games is not ideal preparation for professional sport – but it’s not all bad. “They miss games, the cheque’s still clearing. And you’re trying to tell me they got this kind of addiction to a video game that they sitting there with their thumbs looking like…
body: Smith was hardly an outlier. Other pundits, as well as some Manchester United fans, also questioned Bryan Mbeumo’s focus and professionalism after he posted an image of GTA VI and the word “ historique ” after midnight on Thursday. Meanwhile before last weekend’s Premier League games, the Odd Sport social media account predicted that Chelsea, Brighton and Manchester City would all lose. Why? Because their younger squads might be more focused on Vice City than their opponents, and therefore play with less intensity as a result. By Monday that forecast had been liked tens of thousands of times.

So is there really such a thing as a Grand Theft Auto effect, beyond all the recent hysterics and polemics? The Houston Rockets basketball player Steven Adams certainly thinks so. A couple of months ago he predicted that the launch of GTA VI would cause performances across various leagues to “plummet” in November.

articles.title: Has Verstappen feud reignited at wrong time for Russell?
articles.summary: The reignition of the long-running feud between George Russell and Max Verstappen has added an entertaining twist to the end of the 2026 Formula 1 season, but it may not be what the Mercedes driver needed at this moment.
body: Russell and Verstappen clashed during final practice at the Las Vegas Grand Prix when the Red Bull driver, slightly cheekily, snatched track position from his Mercedes rival as they both prepared for push laps.

Irked by Verstappen's actions, which he later said he felt breached a gentleman's agreement the drivers share, Russell attempted to reclaim track position from the weaving Red Bull, with the pair making slight contact.
The stewards summoned the two drivers following the session as they conducted an investigation, before handing Verstappen a warning.

The incident came less than a month on from Verstappen being involved a similar incident with Racing Bulls driver Liam Lawson during practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix, which resulted in both drivers being given one-place grid penalties.

articles.title: Madness erupts as Sevilla deny Betis in wild end to Spain’s ‘derby of derbies’
articles.summary: Rivals have been heading in opposite directions in recent years but latest clash showed some things never change. “If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said.
body: In the 91st minute of the 146th meeting between Sevilla Fútbol Club and Real Betis Balompié – “derby of derbies” according to Luis García, the Sevilla coach for whom it was the first – Salas’s shot from 18 yards went through Marc Bartra’s legs and Álvaro Valles’s hands. The ball dribbled into the Betis net so apologetically it barely touched the net at all and hadn’t got there before Sevilla’s vice-captain was gone. Raised in Morón de la Frontera, to the south of a city divided, Salas joined Sevilla at 11; now, having levelled the game at 1-1, he went tearing towards the terraces, absolutely losing it like they were.

articles.title: How Northampton are trying to rebuild following takeover involving Pato
articles.summary: They do say the night is darkest before the dawn and that is the great hope at Northampton Town right now. After one of the worst seasons in their history, there were international headlines when a consortium featuring Pato took over in September.
body: In this exclusive interview with Sky Sports, Northampton Town manager Chris Hogg discusses the challenge of turning their fortunes around after relegation last season. A consortium involving Pato offers hope but changing the culture remains the priority...

The former Brazil forward brings a bit of glamour to the Cobblers and their Shoe Army will welcome that. But for Chris Hogg, in his first job as a manager, the day-to-day challenge of turning this struggling football club around continues - and it is hard work.

While the long-term prospects have improved off the pitch, Northampton's revival was always likely to be difficult after such a miserable relegation. It was a dismal season at Sixfields. The campaign completely unravelled, ending with 12 consecutive defeats.

Dropping down a division was never going to make the problems go away. "Relegated teams have found it difficult in League Two. I was very aware of that," Hogg tells Sky Sports. It needed an overhaul, a radical shift in mentality. "Boys with experience of winning."

articles.title: Metcalf denies poking DeJean in the eyes after ejection from Eagles game
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf has denied intentionally poking Philadelphia Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean in the eyes after being ejected from the game during the second half of their 19-16 loss on Sunday.
body: Metcalf was tossed for the third time in his career after being flagged twice for personal fouls following a couple of confrontations with DeJean, the second of which included Metcalf appearing to stick his fingers in between the Eagles defender's facemask.

Asked on Monday if he could go into detail about his exchanges with DeJean, Metcalf initially responded that he "couldn't remember" before backtracking and saying that he was trying to send a message to DeJean to "stop pushing me".
Metcalf had caught only one pass for two yards before being sent to the locker room.
The 28-year-old was suspended for two games last season for swiping at a fan in Detroit and was shown the door twice earlier in his career while playing for the Seattle Seahawks.

articles.title: Pioneer or coach-eater? The complex world of Pozzo's Watford
articles.summary: Pioneering or problematic? Why Gino Pozzo's 14-year Watford ownership is at a crossroads as the club search for their 25th managerial appointment on his watch.
body: A week is said to be a long time in football, and few clubs offer a more compelling test of that theory than Watford.
It has been 14 years since the Pozzo family completed their takeover of the Hornets and Alessio Dionisi's dismissal leaves them searching for the 25th permanent boss of their tenure.
The Italian's dismissal was announced on Sunday lunchtime with his 18th and final game in charge proving to be the 4-0 defeat by Sheffield United less than 24 hours earlier.
An average incumbency of about 210 days per manager has generated all too familiar headlines of the Hornets seeking a new face in the dugout, but is there method in the madness?

articles.title: IFA 'positive' over upgrades needed for World Cup
articles.summary: The Irish Football Association's director of women's football Angela Platt says they are "still working through" plans with the Northern Ireland government to ensure there is funding available to make the necessary upgrades to Windsor Park in time for the 2035 World Cup.
body: It was confirmed on Monday that Northern Ireland, England, Scotland and Wales, the only bidders for the tournament in nine years' time, had been ratified as co-hosts.

Of the 19 venues proposed by the 'All Together' bid, Belfast's Windsor Park is the sole stadium in Northern Ireland, but would require an additional 5,000 seats to its current capacity of 18,500 as well as changes to the pitch and floodlights.

"We're obviously working with our government partners who've committed their support to help us do that, and we'll continue our endeavours to make sure that we work towards that," Platt told BBC NI's Stephen Watson.

"We know that the Northern Ireland Executive has given a commitment to back us and do whatever they can to support us in our endeavours to make sure we're ready for that hosting of the Women's World Cup in 2035.

body: Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya's shoulder injury "doesn't look too serious", but he will miss Tuesday's Champions League against Borussia Dortmund, says Mikel Arteta.
Raya was helped off the pitch in the 70th minute of Arsenal's 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Saturday.
He hurt his left shoulder while claiming a cross and making contact with Newcastle forward William Osula.
"We need some more tests [on Tuesday] but it is quite encouraging," said Gunners boss Arteta.

articles.title: Philadelphia Union Midfielder Cavan Sullivan Wins MLS Young Player Of The Year Award
articles.summary: The award honors the top player who was born Jan. 1, 2004 or later. Sullivan is the youngest player ever to win the award. Red Bull New York had the runner-up and third-place finishers in the voting. Julian Hall finished second and Adri Mehmeti was third.
body: Philadelphia Union midfielder Cavan Sullivan has been selected as the MLS Young Player of the Year for his breakthrough performance as a 17-year-old.

Sullivan had nine goals and 14 assists over 28 games in his first MLS season as a full-time player. He had either a goal or an assist in 10 straight matches, the longest such streak by a teenager in MLS history.
Sullivan was called up to the U.S. men’s national team in September and became the second-youngest player in U.S. history to start a match.
MLS players vote on this award along with club technical staff and media.
